claims.text: The starting material is equiatomic CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy.
Adding Al to CoCrFeNi will promote in-situ formation of an Al2O3 tribofilm during sliding.
The Al2O3 tribofilm will be lubricious.
The Al-containing alloy will maintain low coefficient of friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
The Al-containing alloy will maintain low wear rate from room temperature to 800 °C.
The proposed intervention is to convert CoCrFeNi into an Al-containing CoCrFeNiAl alloy system.
The relevant structural mediator is a continuous Al2O3 layer formed in situ at the sliding interface.
At elevated temperatures, added Al will segregate to the alloy surface.
Surface-segregated Al will oxidize into a thin, continuous Al2O3 film.
The Al2O3 film will reduce friction during sliding.
The Al2O3 film will reduce wear during sliding.
At lower temperatures, the modified alloy microstructure will retain the toughness inherent to the high-entropy alloy.
At lower temperatures, the modified alloy microstructure will retain the wear resistance inherent to the high-entropy alloy.
Self-adaptive oxide formation will mediate sliding performance across the full room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
CoCrFeNiAl will have a consistently lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi across the entire tested temperature range.
CoCrFeNiAl will have a consistently lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi across the entire tested temperature range.
The stated operating boundary is sliding in ambient air from room temperature to 800 °C under the same load and sliding conditions as the baseline.
